messages:
ellen.h: heads up — we're getting a customer escalation: multiple customers reporting 500s from the inference API. I traced some requests and the gateway is returning 500s at the quota check layer instead of 429. Not high overall volume but high impact customers. Can oncall triage? :eyes:

ops-bot: Alert: quota-orchestrator error rate increased >10% in prod-us-east-1 (rule: quota-orch-errrate). 3min window.

sanjay.r: @ellen.h can you paste a sample request id / logs? is this only for specific orgs or widespread?

ellen.h: sample request_id: rq_0a7c3f. Affected orgs: acme-inc (high), beta-saas (medium). Pattern: requests that should be 429 when over quota are being served 500/502 from quota-orchestrator. I grabbed the following log snippet from quota-orch: 

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:21Z] INFO req=rq_0a7c3f org=acme-inc route=/v1/generate stage=quota-check -> call quota-backend
[2026-03-15T09:12:21Z] WARN req=rq_0a7c3f quota-backend timeout=2000ms
[2026-03-15T09:12:21Z] ERROR req=rq_0a7c3f quota-orch error=dep_timeout upstream=quota-gateway code=500 msg="dependency timeout, fallback returned 500"
```

kevin.ops: that looks like quota-gateway timed out and quota-orch didn't map to 429. Do we have a policy that converts dependency failures -> 502/504 vs 4xx? should be 429 for explicit rate limit, but timeouts should probably be 503/504. Need to confirm.

audrey_pm: customer impact: acme reported 35 failed requests in last 10m and they opened a support ticket (INC-8123). They say this started after a deploy ~09:08.

sanjay.r: pinging deploy bot: which deploys around 09:08? I see a runtime deploy for gateway at 09:05 from CI. Could be a circuit-breaker behaviour.

ops-bot: Deploy notification: service=quota-gateway version=rollout-2026-03-15-0902 initiated by=ci-bot at 2026-03-15T09:02:14Z

kevin.ops: ok recreate repro locally: call same endpoint with header x-org=acme-inc and spam until quota exceeded. Also simulate backend slowness with 2s latency to see handling. Use this curl: 

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Org: acme-inc" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

support_jane: I pulled support logs — customers got a 500 JSON body: `\{"error\":\{"code\":500,\"message\":\"quota check failed\"\}}` Not helpful for customers.

sanjay.r: copying internal docs: quota-orch has a mapping layer: if backend returns explicit 4xx (e.g., 429) we forward that. If backend times out or returns 5xx, quota-orch should mark downstream as degraded and return 429 only if we deterministically know over-limit. Looks like current behavior is returning upstream 500 when the backend times out, which is wrong for perceived rate-limit errors. Might be the new deploy changed behaviour to bubble up errors.

ellen.h: Priority: P1 for customer-facing impact. Suggested immediate mitigation: add a temporary edge rewrite that maps quota-orch 5xx -> 429 for known quota paths OR rollback quota-gateway deploy. Which is faster?
\
kevin.ops: rollback is safer if the deploy introduced the change. But rollback could impact other fixes. Edge rewrite can be pushed fast (config change in gateway) to map response.code==500 && route==/v1/generate -> 429 with body explaining transient quota-check fail. I'll prepare a patch.
\
sanjay.r: also check metrics for dependency timeouts on quota-backend: `quota-backend.request_latency.p50/p95`, `quota-orch.dep_timeouts`. If these spiked after 09:02 it's almost certainly the deploy.
\
ops-bot: Metric spike: quota-orch.dep_timeouts increased from 0.1/min to 12/min at 09:06 in prod-us-east-1.
\
kevin.ops: pushing edge rewrite now — patch: `route-mapping: if source_service==quota-orch && response_code>=500 && path=="/v1/generate" -> rewrite status=429 header X-Rate-Limit-Note:"temporary-mapping" body:"rate limit check failed, please retry"` Applying to prod-us-east.
\
ops-bot: Config change applied: route mapping updated (change_id=cfg-9743) at 2026-03-15T09:18:02Z by kevin.ops.
\
support_jane: after config change, customers report 429s with helpful message. Acme confirms failures are now 429 and they can handle gracefully.
\
ellen.h: good. Next: root-cause analysis. Need to decide long-term fix: either ensure quota-orch catches dependency timeouts and returns 429 when appropriate, or make quota-backend resilient. Sanjay and Kevin — can you own a postmortem? Assign to sanjay.r (engineer) and kevin.ops (infra).
\
sanjay.r: will investigate the deploy diff. First suspicion: a change in quota-orch error-handling path that starts surfacing upstream 500s. I'll check PRs merged in last deploy and run replay test against canary.
\
kevin.ops: I'll review gateway mapping surfaced by the deploy and confirm whether a config flag toggled behavior. Also will add a defensive test that simulates quota-backend timeout and asserts response mapping to 4xx/429.
\
audrey_pm: I'll coordinate customer comms: update INC-8123 and note we applied temporary mapping and are working on permanent fix.
\
ellen.h: timeline summary for postmortem: 09:02 deploy rollout-2026-03-15-0902, 09:06 spike in quota dep timeouts, 09:12 support tickets start, 09:18 applied edge rewrite to map 5xx->429, 09:22 customers confirm 429s. Action items: (1) sanjay/kevin postmortem with root cause and fix timeframe (2) add unit/integration tests for mapping (3) add alert runbook update so SREs know to apply mapping quickly.
\
sanjay.r: I'll own item 1 & 2; target EOD.
\
kevin.ops: I'll own item 3 and follow up with a patch to the deploy pipeline to block risky error-handling changes.
\
ellen.h: thanks team. tagging this incident INC-8123 and creating a postmortem doc. If anything else pops up ping here. :thumbsup:
